**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – no documented first-touch-to-first-class pathway (discovery call → payment setup → induction → first class assignment); leaks revenue and creates inconsistent experience
- **Member Checkins** – no cadence or script for retention touchpoints (week 1, month 1, month 3); retention is reactive, not proactive
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no win-back sequence or exit interview process; you're losing data on *why* members leave
- **Health & Safety incident reporting** – no template for injury reports, near-misses, or safeguarding concerns; compliance and liability risk
- **Complaints handling** – no escalation path, response timeframe, or resolution log; legal exposure and member frustration
- **Coach performance feedback loop** – no documented quarterly review or capability conversation process
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – no data retention, access, deletion, or consent audit SOP; regulatory risk
- **Financial reconciliation** – no monthly close-out process for class fees, refunds, and payment disputes
- **Class scheduling conflicts & swaps** – no process for members requesting reschedules or class changes

**Needs updating**

- **Coaching standards SOP** – likely vague on what "quality coaching" looks like; add Class Quality Audit Checklist as appendix with observation rubric (energy, form cueing, personalization, timing)

- **Referral programme SOP** – no tracking mechanism, incentive fulfillment process, or referrer communication cadence

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Map revenue streams first, then price backwards**
Don't start with "what should we charge?" — list every way members currently pay you (memberships, classes, PT sessions, challenges, merchandise, nutrition coaching). For each, document what's *actually* included right now (is PT unlimited? Are certain classes free?). You'll spot gaps and bundling opportunities. Price to your market position, not your costs.

**2. Create two separate, visual documents — not one dense list**
**Coaches' version:** 2-3 pages showing what you *allow* them to offer/upsell, clear pricing guardrails, and what's included in their role (so Sarah doesn't promise something unsustainable). **Members' version:** One-pager visual — membership tiers left-to-right, icons for perks, clear "what's included" boxes. Make it Instagram-story shareable.

**3. Test your menu with 5 members + 2 coaches before finalizing**
Show them drafts this week. Ask: "Does this match what you thought you were paying for?" and "What's missing?" You'll catch disconnect fast — e.g., members think unlimited PT is included when it's not.

**4. Lock pricing for 6 months, communicate the "why"**
Once decided, tell members: "Here's what you get, here's why it costs this, here's when we review." Stops constant price-negotiation friction. Include this in your onboarding doc so new members never wonder.

## REVENUE — CRITICAL ISSUE: MEMBER QUALITY & PRICING COLLAPSE

• **Rev/member has tanked from £145 (July) to £106 (October).** You've added 31 net members (+26%) but revenue per head fell 27%. This signals either heavy discounting on new joiners, or a shift to lower-tier memberships. **Action:** Audit your current pricing tiers and new-member acquisition offers in TeamUp. If new cohorts are on trial/introductory rates, accelerate them to full price or lose margin permanently. Benchmark: you should be targeting £130+ per member/month minimum.

• **September spike (£22k) wasn't repeatable.** October dropped 19% week-on-week despite *higher* active members (167 vs 159). **Action:** Pull September's class attendance data — what drove it (summer retention boost, class schedule change, promo)? Replicate immediately in Nov–Dec.

• **Churn in May was 12.8% — double your normal rate.** Post-relocation disruption likely. Now stable at 3–6%, which is healthy. **But:** you're acquiring members faster than revenue grows, meaning discount or downgrade bias. **Action:** Stop volume-chasing. Tighten new-member onboarding to Premium tier (or add mandatory add-ons: PT sessions, nutrition coaching, merchandise) to restore £140+ ARPU.

• **No upsell revenue visible.** A 167-member gym should generate £2–4k/month in class packs, PT, apparel, supplements. **Action:** Launch a simple retail line (resistance bands, water bottles, protein) or block-book PT sessions (6-week courses at £300–500 each). Low friction, high margin.
